environment.description: Same Spring Boot application deployed in a hardened container on RHEL 9 with a custom SELinux type enforcement policy (logservice_t) compiled and loaded via semodule. The policy confines the java process to logservice_t domain with transitions from container_runtime_t. The type enforcement rules restrict file access to /var/log/appaudit/** (logservice_log_t) and /opt/app/** (logservice_exec_t) only. Network access is constrained to tcp_socket on port 8080 bind/listen/accept. However, the critical control for CRLF is the mandatory confinement of the httpd_response_t object class - the policy includes a custom 'deny' rule on writing to any file labeled httpd_sys_content_t and the container's stdout/response stream is mediated through a local Envoy sidecar proxy (v1.28) configured with an HTTP connection manager that has 'header_sanitization: true' and a custom Lua filter that strips any header value containing bytes 0x0D or 0x0A before forwarding responses to the downstream client. The Envoy listener binds on port 443 (TLS termination) and forwards to localhost:8080.

config.selinux_policy: custom logservice_t type enforcement, deny write to httpd_sys_content_t, confined java domain

envoy_sidecar.lua_filter: function envoy_on_response(response_handle) for k,v in pairs(response_handle:headers()) do if string.find(v, '\r') or string.find(v, '\n') then response_handle:headers():replace(k, string.gsub(string.gsub(v, '\r', ''), '\n', '')) end end end

config.file_access: restricted to /var/log/appaudit/ and /opt/app/ via SELinux TE policy
